transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Alex (Zenwave Head of Platform), Samira (Zenwave Security), Elliot (Zenwave SRE), Jordan (Zenwave Product Ops)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot sync focused on security and compliance gates: SSO test status, audit log fields, data retention mapping, SOC2 evidence needed to progress to pilot sign-off. Short technical check on latency with customer's 8k prompt corpus (Diego to run). Next demo: focused SOC2 mapping + retention spreadsheet.

Topics: SSO/SAML pairing, audit logs schema, data retention/PII flows, SOC2 artifacts, small perf test scheduling, questions about private deployment vs hosted retention controls.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): all right folks let's get started, thanks for joining on time. uh quick roll call?
[00:07] Alex (Zenwave): Alex here.
[00:09] Samira (Zenwave): Samira here.
[00:11] Elliot (Zenwave): Elliot.
[00:12] Jordan (Zenwave): Jordan.
[00:13] Maya (Redwood): great, Maya, Diego, Priya from our side. um agenda is SSO check, audit logs, retention mapping and then a quick perf next steps. sound good?
[00:23] Alex: sounds good. we wanted to prioritize the SOC2 artifacts because our auditors asked for evidence around config and retention.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood CSM): we actually uploaded a starter pack into the shared drive, there's a SOC2 crosswalk doc and an evidence checklist, i'll resend after the call.
[00:37] Samira: i saw the link briefly, thanks. question — for audit logs, what fields do you capture by default? we need to map to our SIEM.
[00:45] Diego (Redwood SE): yeah good question. at a high level we capture request id, timestamp, model id, client id, route, token counts, latencies, and error codes. we also have optional fields for user_id or session_id — those are turned on in private config or as part of enterprise retention.
[01:05] Samira: can you spell that last bit, you said "session id" or "sesson"? the transcript may be off.
[01:10] Diego: session id, s-e-s-s-i-o-n id. and to be clear, PII like raw prompt text is only stored per the retention policy you set — hosted default is 30 days but dedicated/private can be configured to zero retention for content.
[01:24] Elliot: okay so our concern is that even transient prompts could include customer PII, we need to be sure we can redact or not persist. is there an automatic redact step?
[01:32] Diego: we have an optional pre-request filter you can enable that does rule-based redaction — keywords, regexes — and we also support customer-side tokenization or shielded prompt flow where the client strips PII before sending. it's not on by default.
[01:45] Samira: got it. can we get the list of configurable redact rules and whether they're applied at the proxy or inside the runtime?
[01:53] Maya: yes, we'll include that. Diego do you want to note to attach the redact rules doc?
[01:57] Diego: yeah i'll attach the redact rules matrix and note where it runs — primarily at the ingress proxy, with optional runtime hooks.
[02:05] Alex: on SSO — we're trying to get SAML running for our test org. priya, you mentioned test users?
[02:12] Priya: yes i sent SAML metadata yesterday, but i don't think zenwave accepted the metadata yet. we need the identity team to exchange metadata and then we'll validate assertion attributes.
[02:21] Jordan: our side is a bit slow today — i've pushed the SAML metadata to our idp but the attribute mapping is unclear. we need the assertion to include email and an groups claim.
[02:30] Maya: for groups claim we expect either groups or role attribute; we can map whatever you emit, but we need the claim name. samira, can you coordinate with jordan on the exact attribute names?
[02:39] Samira: yes i'll take that.
[02:41] Alex: timeline question — if we resolve SSO and retention mapping this week can we get a pilot sign-off next week? auditors want to see the retention policy in place.
[02:50] Priya: sign-off usually needs SOC2 evidence too — we can produce the configuration export and a screenshot of audit log entries. maya, can redwood produce an evidence export?
[02:59] Maya: yes, we can generate a config export and a time-bounded audit log extract. we'll need to agree on the retention window to pull from.
[03:07] Samira: what format is the audit log extract? json lines or csv?
[03:11] Diego: jsonl is available, csv as well for SIEM ingest. we can add a mapping doc for the field names.
[03:18] Elliot: a quick perf question — diego, you mentioned running our 8k prompt corpus. can that fit into a single batch? we want to replicate production token sizes.
[03:26] Diego: we'll do a staged run; first 1000 prompts to validate correctness, then a full 8k sample. batching will be tuned to keep latency within your SLO. i expect a small number of tail latency spikes with 8k but we'll capture percentiles.
[03:38] Alex: perfect. what do you need from us to run that?
[03:41] Diego: just the corpus as a gzipped jsonl and an API key/test client. we prefer a dedicated test key so we can separate metrics.
[03:48] Jordan: i'll drop that in the secure share after the call.
[03:51] Maya: perfect.
[03:53] Samira: back to SOC2 — any questions about encryption and key management? we use a customer KMS for secrets in a lot of our stack.
[04:01] Maya: for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS via KMS/HSM integrations; hosted can integrate with customer KMS for certain secrets but for hosted you get a managed KMS by default. will include exact flows in the packet.
[04:13] Samira: is the traffic encrypted at rest always? we need to show that to auditors.
[04:17] Diego: yes, data at rest is encrypted. for hosted we use envelope encryption. for private we let you control the root key in your KMS.
[04:24] Alex: about audit log retention — we need logs kept for 12 months for our compliance. will that cost extra?
[04:30] Maya: retention beyond the default window is an enterprise add-on — we can enable 12-month retention for audit logs as part of the pilot contract. i'll include pricing options.
[04:38] Elliot: fine, please include the cost delta.
[04:41] Maya: noted.
[04:43] Samira: small nit — how do you prove deletion when retention is set to zero for content? auditors ask for deletion proof.
[04:49] Diego: we generate a deletion report with a tombstone record and hash of the retained metadata; we'll share the proof template. it's in the SOC2 pack but we'll surface it explicitly.
[04:59] Priya: i'll add that sample deletion report to the drive once diego shares it.
[05:04] Alex: ok, other risk areas?
[05:07] Jordan: we had an internal question about model fallback — if a hosted model is not available and you fall back to a cheaper variant, does that change data locality or logs?
[05:18] Maya: good question. our routing preserves tenancy and region — fallback only switches model variant within the same compliance boundary; audit logs still include the fallback event and model id. we'll document the fallback semantics.
[05:30] Samira: please show that in the evidence packet. auditors like concrete samples.
[05:34] Diego: also, for the perf run I'll annotate logs with trace ids so you can match requests end-to-end.
[05:41] Alex: awesome. next, can we do a brief run through of the evidence packet contents just to confirm?
[05:46] Maya: yes — config export (roles+policies), audit log sample, encryption/KMS notes, deletion report template, SSO assertion example, retention matrix.
[05:55] Samira: that covers it.
[05:57] Priya: i'll create a short checklist and share with alex so we can cross off items.
[06:02] Maya: great. any blockers?
[06:05] Samira: SAML attribute names — we'll sort this today.
[06:08] Jordan: corpus will be uploaded after this call.
[06:10] Diego: i'll schedule the perf run for Thursday and share results by next Monday.
[06:15] Alex: perfect.
[06:17] Maya: recap of next steps: maya to share SOC2 packet & retention matrix by friday (2026-05-08); diego to run perf and share latency/cost sheet; samira to send attribute mapping; priya to coordinate SSO test users.
[06:33] Alex: that works for us. thanks team.
[06:35] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with links and the action items.
[06:40] [call ends]

References / shared links noted in call:
- SOC2 crosswalk (Redwood): https://redwood.example.com/soc2/zenwave-crosswalk (will be shared post-call)
- Redaction rules matrix (to attach)

Action items repeated:
- Maya Patel: share SOC2 evidence packet & retention options (due 2026-05-08)
- Diego Rivera: run 8k prompt perf test and provide latency/cost results (due 2026-05-14)
- Samira Khan: provide SAML attribute names and audit log field requirements (due 2026-05-12)

End of transcript.
